mn19:1.2: On one occasion the Blessed One was living at Sāvatthi in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapindika’s Park.
mn19:1.3: There he addressed the bhikkhus thus:
mn19:2.1: ‘Bhikkhus, before my enlightenment, while I was still only an unenlightened Bodhisatta, it occurred to me:
mn19:2.2: “Suppose that I divide my thinking into two classes?”
mn19:2.3: Then I set on one side thinking with sensual desires, thinking with ill-will, and thinking with cruelty,
mn19:2.5: and I set on the other side thinking with renunciation, thinking with non-ill-will, and thinking with non-cruelty.
mn19:3.1: ‘As I dwelt thus, diligent, ardent and self-controlled, thinking with sensual desire arose in me.
mn19:3.3: “There is this thinking with sensual desire arisen in me.
mn19:3.4: And that leads to my own affliction, to others’ affliction and to the affliction of both; it obstructs understanding, promotes annoyance, and leads away from Nibbāna.”
mn19:3.5: When I considered: “This leads to my own affliction”, it subsided in me;
mn19:3.6: when I considered: “This leads to others’ affliction”, it subsided in me;
mn19:3.7: when I considered: “This leads to the affliction of both”, it subsided in me;
mn19:3.8: when I considered: “This obstructs understanding, promotes annoyance and leads away from Nibbāna”, it subsided in me.
mn19:3.9: Whenever thinking with sensual desire arose in me, I abandoned it, removed it, did away with it.
mn19:4-5.1: ‘As I dwelt thus, diligent, ardent and self-controlled, thinking with ill-will arose in me … I abandoned it, removed it, did away with it.
mn19:4-5.2: ‘As I dwelt thus, diligent, ardent, and self-controlled, thinking with cruelty arose in me … I abandoned it, removed it, did away with it.
mn19:6.1: ‘In whatever way a bhikkhu keeps thinking and pondering, that will effect the inclination of his mind accordingly.
mn19:6.2: ‘If he keeps thinking with sensual desire and pondering with sensual desire, he has abandoned thinking with renunciation to cultivate thinking with sensual desire, and then his mind is inclined to thinking with sensual desire.
mn19:6.3: ‘If he keeps thinking with ill-will … his mind his mind is inclined to thinking with ill-will.
mn19:6.4: ‘If he keeps thinking with cruelty … his mind is inclined to thinking with cruelty.
mn19:7.1: ‘Just as, in the last month of the Rains, in the autumn season when the crops thicken, a herdsman would guard his cows
mn19:7.2: (constantly) tapping and poking them on this side and that with a stick to check and curb them.
mn19:7.4: Because he foresees the flogging or imprisonment or loss or blame that could befall (him if he let them stray into the crops),
mn19:7.5: so too, I foresaw in unprofitable dhammas a danger of degradation and defilement, and in profitable dhammas a blessing in renunciation, which blessing is on the side of cleansing.
mn19:8.1: ‘As I dwelt thus, diligent, ardent and self-controlled thinking with renunciation arose in me.
mn19:8.3: “There is this thinking with renunciation arisen in me.
mn19:8.4: And that does not lead to my own affliction, or to others’ affliction or to the affliction of both, it aids understanding, does not promote annoyance and leads to Nibbāna.
mn19:8.5: If I think with that and ponder with that even for a night,
mn19:8.7: even for a night and day, I foresee nothing to fear from it:
mn19:8.8: only that with the continuous thinking and pondering I might tire my body,
mn19:8.9: and a tired body harries the mind,
mn19:8.10: and a harried mind is far from concentration.”
mn19:8.11: (Accordingly), I settled mind in myself, quieted it, brought it to singleness and concentrated it.
mn19:8.13: So that my mind should not be harried.
mn19:9-10.1: ‘As I dwelt thus, diligent ardent and self-controlled, thinking with non-ill-will arose in me … my mind should not be harried.
mn19:9-10.2: ‘As I dwelt thus, diligent, ardent and self-controlled, thinking with non-cruelty arose in me … my mind should not be harried.
mn19:11.1: ‘In whatever way a bhikkhu keeps thinking and pondering, that will affect the inclination of his mind accordingly.
mn19:11.2: ‘If he keeps thinking with renunciation and pondering with renunciation, he has abandoned thinking with sensual desire to cultivate thinking with renunciation, and then his mind is inclined to thinking with renunciation.
mn19:11.3: ‘If he keeps thinking with non-ill-will … his mind is inclined to thinking with non-ill-will.
mn19:11.4: ‘If he keeps thinking with non-cruelty … his mind is inclined to thinking with non-cruelty.
mn19:12.1: ‘Just as in the last month of the Heat, when all the crops have been brought inside the villages, a herdsman would guard his cows while staying at the root of a tree out in the open since he needs only to be mindful that
mn19:12.3: so too there was need for me only to be mindful that
mn19:13.1: 11-22. ‘Tireless energy was aroused in me (as in Sutta 4, para. 22-33) as (happens) in one who abides diligent, ardent and self-controlled.
mn19:25.1: ‘Suppose that in a wooded range there was a great low-lying marsh,
mn19:25.2: near which a big herd of deer lived,
mn19:25.3: and then a man appeared seeking what was not their good, their welfare, their surcease of bondage,
mn19:25.4: and he closed the safe and good path that led to their happiness and opened a false path, and he put out a decoy and set up a dummy,
mn19:25.5: so that later on the big herd of deer might come to loss, ruin and calamity;
mn19:25.6: but suppose some man came seeking their good, their welfare, their surcease of bondage,
mn19:25.7: and he reopened the safe and good path that led to their happiness and closed the false path, and he harried away the decoy and destroyed the dummy,
mn19:25.8: so that later on the big herd of deer might come to growth, increase and fulfilment.
mn19:26.1: ‘Bhikkhus, I have given you this simile in order to intimate a meaning.
mn19:26.2: Now the meaning here is this:
mn19:26.3: The great low-lying marsh stands for sensual desires;
mn19:26.4: the big herd of deer stands for beings,
mn19:26.5: the man who sought what was not their good, their happiness and their surcease of bondage stands for Māra the Evil One;
mn19:26.6: the false path stands for the wrong Eightfold Path, that is to say,
mn19:26.7: wrong view, wrong intention, wrong speech, wrong action, wrong livelihood, wrong effort, wrong mindfulness, wrong concentration,
mn19:26.8: the decoy stands for delight and lust,
mn19:26.10: the man seeking their good, their happiness and their surcease of bondage stands for the Tathāgata, Arahant and Full Enlightened,
mn19:26.11: the safe and good path that led to their happiness stands for the Noble Eightfold Path, that is to say,
mn19:26.12: right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right concentration.
mn19:26.13: ‘So, bhikkhus, the safe and good path that leads to happiness has been reopened by me, the wrong path has been closed, the decoy harried away, and the dummy destroyed.’
mn19:27.1: ‘What should be done for his disciples out of pity by a Master who seeks their welfare and has pity (on them), that I have done for you.
mn19:27.2: There these roots of trees, these empty huts. Develop meditation, bhikkhus, do not delay lest you later regret it. This is our message to you.’
mn19:27.3: That is what the Blessed One said.
mn19:27.4: The bhikkhus were satisfied, and they delighted in the Blessed One’s words.
